---
name: or-motion-scene
description: Author, validate and materialise a deterministic MotionScene in the open OR project — code-to-illustration, animated titles, diagrams, reusable scene JSON and the app's motion library. Use when the user asks for an illustration, motion graphic or scene from code. Do NOT use for ordinary edits (or-timeline-edit) or for changing OR's own MotionScene implementation.
---

# Motion scene

Workspace guide: `docs/motion-scenes.md`. The app's motion library is recorded in
`project.json` as `motion_library_path`, so every motion verb resolves it from
`--attach project.json`; `--library PATH` overrides it for one call.

## Procedure

1. Decide the input: a source file (code illustration) or an authored
   `.ormotion.json` (title, diagram, reusable scene).
2. For a scene, start from `node tools/motion-scaffold.mjs --name "Title"
   --out scenes/title.ormotion.json`, then edit nodes, text, colours, sizes,
   keyframes and the camera move.
3. Validate with `tools/or motion validate --file scenes/title.ormotion.json
   --json`. Fix every diagnostic; do not render a scene that fails validation.
   Read the composition with `tools/or motion layout --file ... --at 1/2
   --json`; the node boxes are the layout, so do not ask for a screenshot.
4. Publish it with `tools/or motion publish --attach project.json --scene
   scenes/title.ormotion.json --json` (or `--source`). One call validates,
   renders, imports the video, inserts an ordinary clip and saves the scene as a
   reusable library asset; pass `--no-library` when the library copy is not wanted.
   Materialisation encodes every frame: wait for the result and never run two at
   once.
5. Verify the clip appears with `tools/or timeline clips --track TRACK_ID
   --attach project.json --json`, then `tools/or project save --attach
   project.json --json` unless the user asked to review first.

## Rules

- The scene is declarative and bounded: no expressions, scripts, network assets
  or provider calls. Refer to assets by scene-local or project-relative path.
- Flat colour only (3–5 fills), at least two animations running across the whole
  scene, short Vietnamese titles with their diacritics intact (NFC; the renderer
  picks Inter for ASCII and Be Vietnam Pro for non-ASCII), and no empty static
  middle. The scaffold starts from that shape. Read the boxes with `motion
  layout` instead of trusting a still.
- `publish` refuses a scene with image assets; the app's Motion panel publishes
  those. Keep image material in the library and insert it from the app.
- Text is literal; changing the title means changing the `text` field.
- A re-render never replaces the existing clip. Insert the new render and remove
  the old clip only when the user asks.
- Keep scenes short; a long scene is slow to encode and hard to revise.
- Library verbs take `--attach project.json` and resolve the folder from the
  pointer: `motion asset list`, `validate --file`, `save --file`,
  `instantiate --id --output`, `import --source PNG`, `remove --id`, and
  `insert --asset-id ID [--values JSON]` (insert also renders through the app).
  `--library PATH` overrides the folder for one call. Do not copy or edit library
  files yourself. Use the `mcp__or__motion_*` tools only if the CLI call fails and
  its error does not explain why.

## Report

State the scene file, its duration and canvas, the track and time the clip was
inserted at, whether a library asset was saved, and whether the project was saved.

name: or-project-safety
description: Protect the open OR project while editing — check revision and dirty state, save explicitly, undo or redo canonical history through the workspace or CLI, handle refused commands and report honestly. Use before any save, undo or recovery decision, or when a project command fails unexpectedly. Do NOT use for designing OR's history or command model.

# Project safety

Workspace guide: `docs/project-safety.md`.

## Procedure

1. Before changing anything, read `tools/or project summary --attach project.json
   --json` for the revision, and `tools/or session describe --attach project.json
   --json` for `dirty` when the save state matters.
2. After the requested change, read the affected state (`timeline clips` or
   `media list`).
3. Save once with `tools/or project save --attach project.json --json` unless the
   user asked to review first.
4. If the user wants a change undone, use `tools/or history undo --attach
   project.json --json` and say how many edits it covered. A `--apply` voiceover
   run is several edits, not one.
5. Never close, shut down, recover or reset the project: `session shutdown` and
   `recovery status|apply|discard` are the user's actions. `session describe` is a
   read and is fine.

## Rules

- Never write a `.orproj` file or any project path directly.
- A revision conflict or refused command: re-read, retry once with real values,
  then stop and report.
- A locked track is a refusal with a cause: read `timeline tracks`, ask before
  clearing the lock, then edit.
- A missing CLI verb for speed, volume, styling or export is the app's surface,
  not a failure; say so instead of working around it.
- `dirty` is evidence. If an edit succeeded but the project is not dirty, report
  the inconsistency instead of claiming success.
- Do not invent command success. Every claim names the verb and the state you read.

---
name: or-script-production
description: Plan and produce a narrated OR edit offline — write an or-assistant-script, generate macOS say voiceover, derive exact caption clips, and add a generated music bed, while leaving cloud voices, recording and speech models to the app. Use when the user asks for a script, voiceover/dubbing, automatic subtitles for audio, or background music. Do NOT use for ordinary timeline edits (or-timeline-edit) or for changing OR's own implementation.
---

# Script production

Read `docs/script-and-voice.md` for the exact formats and command lines, and
`docs/audio-prep.md` when the audio itself needs recording, clean-up or a speech
model. This skill is the working order; the guides are the reference.

## 1. Fix the brief before writing

Ask for, or confirm from the request: length in seconds, language (`vi` or
`en`), audience, tone, voice, and music mood. If the user asked for a 30-second
video, do not write a 90-second script. If the user names a cloud voice, say the
app generates that one: **Audio → Generate voiceover…** uses the voice from
**Settings → Narration**, whose provider keys live in the keychain and never
enter this workspace.

## 2. Write one line per scene

Save `work/scripts/<slug>.json` with `format: "or-assistant-script"`,
`schema_version: 1`, and a `scenes` array. Each scene has a unique kebab-case
`id`, a short `narration`, an optional `caption`, and an optional `marker`. Keep
each line to one sentence or two; split long paragraphs.

## 3. Validate before speaking

```sh
node tools/voiceover.mjs --script work/scripts/<slug>.json --plan --json
```

Fix format errors and read the planned timings back to the user if the total is
far from the requested length.

## 4. Narrate and caption

Preferred one-step path when the user wants it in the edit:

```sh
node tools/voiceover.mjs --script work/scripts/<slug>.json \
  --out work/voiceover/<slug> --apply --attach project.json --json
```

Without `--apply`, generate only, report the manifest/`captions.srt`, and let
the user listen first. When you use `--apply`, confirm the result with `timeline
tracks` and `timeline clips` before saving, and say it is several edits, not one
undo step.

## 5. Add music

```sh
node tools/music.mjs --out work/music/<slug>.wav --duration <seconds> --mood <mood> --json
```

Import it, place it on an audio track, and tell the user the bed is intentionally
quiet and adjustable in the inspector. Do not raise the generated level. Ducking
under the voice is one `timeline duck-clip` command, or one click in the app's
Music dialog.

## 6. Finish

Add the visuals the user asked for, review the timeline, then `project save`.
Report which parts came from the script (narration and captions) and which from
transcription or generation, and what remains unverified.

## Existing audio instead of a script

If the user already has audio or video, use `tools/or captions transcribe
--attach project.json --media MEDIA_ID --srt-out PATH`, review the cues, then
`tools/or timeline import-captions --file PATH`. It needs the running app and the
model the app has installed; if it reports `TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`, ask
the user to open **Audio → Speech model…** once instead of downloading a model
yourself. Caption styling (font, size, anchor, offset, box, opacity) has no CLI
verb; that is the app's Edit Caption dialog.

## Checks

- `--plan` is side-effect free; use it after every script edit.
- `say` and the music generator are offline; never claim a network call, and never
  claim a cloud voice when the system voice spoke.
- A `--apply` failure leaves an unsaved edit; inspect with `timeline tracks`
  before deciding whether to undo or retry.
- Never save a stale revision: if a command reports a revision conflict, read
  `project summary` and re-apply the remaining steps.

name: or-timeline-edit
description: Make one timeline change in the open OR project through the workspace or CLI — add, insert, move, trim, slip, roll, slide, split, delete, re-time or mark clips, tracks and the sequence. Use when the user asks for an edit to the timeline. Do NOT use for media import (read docs/media-and-import.md), MotionScene authoring (or-motion-scene), or developing OR itself.

# Timeline edit

Workspace guide: `docs/timeline-editing.md`.

## Procedure

1. `tools/or project summary --attach project.json --json` — confirm the project
   and read the revision.
2. `tools/or timeline tracks|settings|markers --attach project.json --json` and
   `tools/or timeline clips --track TRACK_ID` — read rates, tracks with their
   state, clips and markers. Use only ids and times from these results. Clips and
   markers page: pass `--offset` while the result reports more.
3. Choose the smallest command. If the target track does not exist, create it with
   `timeline add-track`; text and caption clips need a text or caption track. A
   locked track refuses edits: ask before clearing the lock with
   `timeline set-track-state`.
4. Run it with `--attach project.json --json` and exact `NUM/DEN` or decimal times.
5. Re-read the track when placement matters, then `tools/or project save
   --attach project.json --json` unless the user asked to review first.

## Rules

- One requested change per turn; do not bundle unrequested edits.
- Never invent ids or times from the prompt. The panel context names the current
  clip and playhead only when they exist.
- `--mode insert` moves later clips right; `--mode overwrite` clears the range.
  Say which one you used.
- Slip moves the source window inside a fixed clip, roll moves the cut to its
  neighbour, slide moves the clip and lets the neighbours absorb it. They take a
  signed `--delta`, not an absolute time.
- `--ripple` on `trim-clip` is accepted on the end edge only.
- Speed, reverse, freeze, clip volume, mute, title/caption styling, group move,
  effects and export have no CLI verb. Say the app owns them (timeline strip,
  inspector, dialog, Export) and let the user make that change; never fake it with
  a trim or a split.
- When this workspace has no `project.json` to attach through, use the matching
  `mcp__or__*` tool and say so.
- A refused edit is information: re-read, retry once with valid values, then
  report.

## Report

Name the track, the clip and the exact time that changed, and whether the project
was saved.

# OR Agent Workspace

This is the operating workspace the Opencut Reinforced assistant uses by default.
It is not the OR source checkout. The open project is recorded in `project.json`,
and the `or` CLI attached through that pointer is the default way to read or
change it. The `mcp__or__*` tools are a fallback for motion insertion, the motion
library, and a CLI failure whose error does not explain itself.

## Rule

Read the smallest entry that answers the current task. Do not preload the guides:
each line below names the situation that makes it the right thing to read.

## Routing

### Guides

- **Full video pipeline (default for a complete video)** — local narration,
  beat-planned MotionScenes with baked captions, parallel scene materialisation,
  music and one assembly pass into the open project.
  When: the user asks for a whole video, explainer, narrated sequence, montage or
  any multi-scene piece built from motion graphics. Start here instead of
  authoring scenes one at a time, and keep `render.mjs` at 3 workers unless the
  machine is idle. Path: `templates/video-pipeline/README.md`
- **Timeline editing** — tracks and their state, clips, markers, slip/roll/slide and sequence commands with exact times.
  When: the user asks to add, move, trim, slip, roll, slide, split, delete, reorder, re-time or mark something on the timeline.
  Path: `docs/timeline-editing.md`
- **Media and import** — media ids, probing, importing, paging, source relinking and removal.
  When: the task needs a file in the library before it can be placed, or needs an existing media id.
  Path: `docs/media-and-import.md`
- **Motion scenes** — code-to-video scenes, `.ormotion.json`, camera, the scene scaffold, validation, materialisation and the reusable asset library.
  When: the user asks for an illustration, motion graphic, animated title or scene from code, or a reusable scene asset.
  Path: `docs/motion-scenes.md`
- **Project safety** — revisions, save, undo/redo, rename, refused commands and the verbs that are not the agent's to call.
  When: deciding whether to save, undoing a change, or recovering from a failed command.
  Path: `docs/project-safety.md`
- **Script, narration and music** — an `or-assistant-script`, offline macOS
  voiceover, exact caption clips, generated background music, and the rule that
  cloud narration happens in the app.
  When: the user asks for a script, voiceover/dubbing, or background music.
  Path: `docs/script-and-voice.md`
- **Audio prep** — recording a take in the app, cleaning noise from a file, choosing a speech model and transcribing existing audio.
  When: the audio itself is the problem — too noisy, needs recording, or needs subtitles from what was said.
  Path: `docs/audio-prep.md`
- **Troubleshooting** — missing tools, no open project, refused scenes, missing motion library, failed transcription, slow or failed renders.
  When: a command fails and the error is not self-explanatory.
  Path: `docs/troubleshooting.md`

### Skills

The session catalog carries these. Load one only when its task matches.

- `or-timeline-edit` — orient, act, verify and save one timeline change, including
  track state, slip/roll/slide and markers.
- `or-motion-scene` — author, validate and materialise a deterministic scene, and
  place a reusable asset.
- `or-project-safety` — protect revisions, respect locked tracks, and report edits
  honestly.
- `or-script-production` — plan a script, narrate it offline, derive exact captions
  and add a generated music bed.

### Tools

- `tools/or` — the OR CLI bound to this app build and the default project surface.
  Run it from this workspace: `tools/or <verb> --attach project.json --json`.
  `project.json` is the app-written session pointer; the CLI follows its
  `descriptor_path`, so the same command line keeps working when another project
  opens. `tools/or commands` and `tools/or queries` print the exact verb surface.
- `tools/or motion publish` — validate, render through the app, import and insert a
  scene in one call. `project.json` records the app's motion library, so the call
  also saves the scene as a reusable asset; `--no-library` skips that on purpose.
  `tools/or motion asset validate|list|save|instantiate|insert|import|remove`
  reads and writes the same library: pass `--attach project.json` and the CLI
  resolves the folder from the pointer, while `--library PATH` overrides it for one
  call. The `mcp__or__motion_*` tools are a fallback for a CLI failure whose error
  does not explain itself; report the failure before switching.
- `tools/or media clean-audio --source IN --out OUT --json` — offline noise
  reduction that writes a new file; import it to use it. The app's media menu does
  the same in one step.
- `tools/or captions transcribe` / `tools/or timeline import-captions` — local
  multilingual transcription of existing audio, and applying reviewed cues as a
  caption track. Transcription needs the running app and the model the app has
  installed. This is the "subtitles from audio" path.
- `tools/motion-scaffold.mjs` — writes a valid V1 `.ormotion.json` skeleton with a
  camera move:
  `node tools/motion-scaffold.mjs --name "Title" --out scenes/title.ormotion.json`.
- `tools/voiceover.mjs` — validates an `or-assistant-script`, speaks it with the
  macOS voice, writes a timing manifest and SRT, and can import/place/caption the
  result with `--apply`:
  `node tools/voiceover.mjs --script work/scripts/demo.json --plan --json`.
- `tools/music.mjs` — synthesises a quiet, royalty-free background bed offline.
  A prompt is read the same way as the app's Generate music dialog; flags are the
  fallback and override it:
  `node tools/music.mjs --out work/music/bed.wav --prompt "nhạc nền nhẹ nhàng 30 giây, không trống" --json`.

## Working files

- `scenes/` — scene sources you author. `tools/or motion publish --scene` reads them.
- `work/` — scratch files, notes and copies. Nothing here is project state.
- `project.json`, `or-cli.json` and `tools/or` are written by the app; leave them
  alone. `project.json` names the live descriptor the CLI attaches through, the
  `motion_library_path` the motion verbs resolve and the `app_support_path` other
  app preferences are read from.

## Bounds

- Never edit a `.orproj` file, the project directory, or any path listed in `project.json`.
- Project mutations go through `tools/or ... --attach project.json`; the app applies
  them and owns history. The motion MCP tools are a fallback write path, not the
  default.
- Never read, ask for or store a cloud provider key. Narration keys live in the
  macOS keychain and belong to the app's Settings → Narration panel.
- Playback speed, clip volume, title and caption styling, export, microphone
  recording, cloud voices and the speech-model picker are app-only: say which
  surface owns the request instead of inventing a command, and never fake one
  with a trim, a split or a duplicate clip.
- Make one requested change at a time, confirm it with a timeline read, then save
  unless the user asked to review first.

# Audio prep

Scope: audio the user records or already has, made usable before it becomes
narration, captions or a music bed. The script path is
[script-and-voice.md](script-and-voice.md); placing the result is
[timeline-editing.md](timeline-editing.md).

## Record a take — the app owns the microphone

The workspace has no audio capture. The Audio tool's **Record voice…** dialog
records one take with the system microphone, writes it under
`<application support>/voice-recordings`, and on accept imports it and places it
as an ordinary audio clip. When the user asks to record, say the app does it;
afterwards read `media list` and the new audio track instead of guessing a path.

A recorded take is the sample an ElevenLabs personal voice is created from, but
that creation happens in **Settings → Narration** and is the user's action.

## Clean up noise

Two surfaces, one behaviour: write a new file, then import it as its own media
item so the original stays available for comparison.

- In the app: a media item's menu → **Clean up Audio**. It measures the floor,
  reduces 12 dB, writes a `.cleaned.wav` file into
  `<application support>/audio-cleanup/` and imports the result.
- In the workspace, file to file:

```sh
tools/or media clean-audio --source /absolute/in.wav --out /absolute/out.wav --json
```

`--noise-floor-db` (whole dBFS) and `--reduction` (whole dB, 12 by default) are
optional. Without `--noise-floor-db` the tool measures the recording's own floor
first, because a constant either does nothing or eats the voice. The JSON result's
`cleanup` block reports the floor it used, the reduction, the bytes written and
the filter chain.

The clean-up runs through the packaged FFmpeg helper and opens no project, so
nothing changes in the project until you import the output:

```sh
tools/or media add --attach project.json --source /absolute/out.wav --json
```

If the helper is missing (a plain debug CLI), the verb fails with a helper error:
say so and point the user at the app's **Clean up Audio** action rather than
retrying.

Clean-up can thin a voice or dull music. Compare before replacing: leave the
original clip in place, place the cleaned item where the user asked, and let them
choose. Never delete or mute the original unless asked.

## Speech models and transcription

The model belongs to the app, not the workspace. **Audio → Speech model…**
chooses one of five multilingual checkpoints (Base 141 MiB, Small 465 MiB,
Medium 1.43 GiB, Large v3 Turbo q5 547 MiB, Large v3 Turbo 1.51 GiB), downloads
it once after explicit consent, verifies it by size and SHA-256, and keeps it in
the app's private folder. The picker shows the installed total and can remove a
model; removing the active one falls back to the catalog default. `or captions
transcribe` and the MCP tool reuse that choice.

```sh
tools/or captions transcribe --attach project.json --media MEDIA_ID \
  --srt-out work/captions/clip.srt --json
tools/or timeline import-captions --attach project.json \
  --file work/captions/clip.srt --json
```

Transcription needs the running app: `--project PATH` is refused with a message
saying so. It decodes audio locally, detects Vietnamese or English, changes no
project state, and returns bounded cues with `start_ms`, `end_ms`, `text` and the
detected `language`. Review them, fix the SRT if needed, then import; the import
creates one caption track with one editable clip per cue.

`TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` means no model is installed or the runtime is
not in this build. Do not download a model from the workspace: ask the user to
open **Speech model…** once (or install the local helper binaries with
`scripts/install_local_transcription_helpers.sh`).

## Bounds

- No credentials: cloud voice keys live in the macOS keychain and belong to the
  app's Settings, not to this workspace.
- No model weights, no network call, no microphone from the CLI.
- Clean-up output and transcripts are files under `work/` until imported; they are
  not project state.
- Never claim a recording, a transcription or a cleaned file exists because a
  command was attempted; read `media list` and the caption track back.

# Media and import

Scope: getting a file into the project library, finding the id the timeline
commands take, and keeping sources findable. The library is project state;
importing is a project mutation and is saved like any other edit.

## Order of operations

1. `tools/or media list --attach project.json --json` — check whether the file is
   already imported. The list is paged: pass `--offset` while the page reports
   more items.
2. `tools/or media add --attach project.json --source PATH --json` — import an
   **absolute** path. The result carries the new media id and its metadata.
3. Place it with `timeline insert-clip` (see
   [timeline-editing.md](timeline-editing.md)); use the duration from this result.
4. `tools/or project save --attach project.json --json` after the edit, unless the
   user asked to review first.

## Verbs

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `media probe --file PATH` | Read one file's metadata without a project or an app session. |
| `media list [--offset N] [--limit N]` | Read the library page by page. |
| `media add --source PATH` | Import one absolute path; returns the new media id and metadata. |
| `media relink --id MEDIA_ID --source PATH` | Point an existing item at a new source under the same `MediaId`; undoable, and timeline references survive. |
| `media remove --id MEDIA_ID` | Remove a library entry; refused while a clip references it. |
| `media clean-audio --source PATH --out PATH [--noise-floor-db N] [--reduction N]` | Noise reduction that reads one file and writes another. Nothing in the project changes until the result is imported; see [audio-prep.md](audio-prep.md). |

## What can be imported

- The supported profile is Matroska (FFV1/PCM S16LE, VP9/Opus, H.264/AAC), WAV
  PCM S16LE, MP3 audio and WebM VP9/Opus. MP4-family H.264/AAC import is a
  candidate profile; H.265 and AV1 are not supported.
- A file must exist and be readable when `media add` runs; the library records a
  source path, not a copy.
- Importing the same path twice is allowed; use the id the new call returns.
- An unsupported file is reported as unsupported, not corrupt. A probe that the
  packaged `ffprobe` cannot complete falls back to the libavformat the app links,
  so a QuickTime file the helper rejects can still import.

## Paths

- `--source` must be absolute. The workspace sits outside the project, so a path
  relative to the project is not automatically correct.
- Files the agent downloaded or wrote live under `work/`; keep them there and pass
  that absolute path.
- Do not move or delete a source file after importing it. If it moves, relink it
  with `media relink`; do not import it again unless the user wants a second copy.
- `media remove` removes a library entry, not the file on disk.

## Reading metadata

`media list` returns ids, source paths, duration, dimensions and audio details.
Use the returned duration when a clip needs a length; do not round it into a
different time base. `media probe` answers the same questions for a file that is
not in the project yet and needs the packaged FFmpeg helper; if that helper is
missing, the command reports a helper error and the app still imports the file.
`project summary` reports the project revision; `session describe` adds the
`dirty` save state.

# Motion scenes

Scope: turning code or a declarative `.ormotion.json` scene into an ordinary,
editable video clip through the app's deterministic MotionScene renderer. No
provider or network call happens here.

## Two inputs

| Input | Use |
|---|---|
| A source file | `tools/or motion publish --attach project.json --source work/sample.rs --name "Parser" --json` turns the code into a highlighted illustration. |
| A scene file | `tools/or motion publish --attach project.json --scene scenes/title.ormotion.json --json` renders an authored scene. |

Pass exactly one of `--source` and `--scene`. One call validates the scene,
renders it through the app, imports the result, inserts an ordinary clip and saves
the scene as a reusable library asset (see below). It is slow because every frame
is encoded; do not start a second render while one is running and do not retry
after a timeout without checking the timeline.

`publish` accepts vector scenes only. A scene with image `assets` is refused: the
app's Motion panel publishes those, because it copies the images into the library.

Useful optional arguments: `--title` (the generated scene's title for a `--source`
run), `--name`, `--category`, `--at`, `--track`, `--width`, `--height`,
`--frame-rate` (`30/1`), `--output`, `--library`, `--no-library`. When `--at` is
omitted the clip is appended after the target track; when `--track` is omitted the
first unlocked video track is used, and one is created when the project has none.
`--output` must be absolute and defaults to `<project folder>/generated/`.
`materialize` remains available when only a file is wanted; it never imports or
inserts.

## The motion library folder

The app keeps its library at `<application support>/motion-library`, and the
workspace `project.json` records that path as `motion_library_path`. Every motion
verb attached through the pointer therefore finds the same library the app shows:
`tools/or motion asset list --attach project.json --json` needs no other flag, and
`publish` saves the scene as a reusable asset by default. `--library PATH`
overrides the folder for one call; pass `--no-library` when a library copy is
genuinely not wanted. Do not copy or edit library files yourself.

If a pointer written by an older build has no library entry, the CLI says so:
reconnect the assistant so the app rewrites `project.json`, or pass `--library`.

## Authoring a scene

Start from the scaffold, then edit the JSON:

```sh
node tools/motion-scaffold.mjs --name "Title" --out scenes/title.ormotion.json \
  [--width 1920] [--height 1080] [--seconds 4]
```

Validate before rendering:

```sh
tools/or motion validate --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --json
```

`tools/or motion inspect` summarises nodes and animation counts;
`tools/or motion layout --file ... --at 1/2 --json` lists every node's evaluated
box (position, size, rotation, opacity, text, animated flag) at one exact time —
this is how you read the composition, without a screenshot. `tools/or motion
evaluate --file ... --at 1/2` shows the resolved paint instructions. Neither
touches a project or the encoder. `tools/or motion render` rasterises one frame to
a PNG when a still is enough. `tools/or motion from-code` writes a scene from a
source file without materialising it, so the agent can adjust the generated scene
first.

`tools/or motion materialize --attach project.json --source PATH --output
<absolute .mkv>` renders to disk through the live app but does not import or
insert the result; use it only when a file is wanted, never as an insertion path.

## Design rules (learned from the slideshow failure)

- **Flat colour only.** Pick three to five flat fills and reuse them; do not
  fake a gradient with stacked bands. The format has no gradient and reviewers
  read bands as a mistake.
- **Never a dead frame.** Keep two or three animations running across the whole
  duration — a slow drift, a pulse, a wipe — not only entrance fades. If the
  middle of the scene is static, it reads as a slide.
- **Type first.** Titles are at most six or seven words per line at 1080p, at
  least 28 px, with a 5 % margin. ASCII lines use Inter; a line with Vietnamese
  or any non-ASCII character uses Be Vietnam Pro, the bundled display face, so
  stacked marks keep their shape. Write NFC text, never strip diacritics to fit,
  and never pick a font name — both faces are bundled and the renderer chooses.
  Wrapping and shrinking to 60 % are safety nets, not a layout choice.
- **Cut on movement.** Overlap the end of one idea with the start of the next;
  avoid a fully empty frame between beats.
- **A camera move is the cheapest life.** A slow push-in (`camera.keyframes`
  with `zoom` 1 → 1.08, a small pan) keeps every frame moving; keep zoom ≥ 1 so
  a flat background never shows the canvas edge.
- Read the result with `tools/or motion layout --file ... --at MID --json`; the
  boxes are what a viewer sees, so check that text stays inside its canvas.

## Envelope

```json
{
  "format": "opencut-reinforced-motion-scene",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "scene_id": "<UUIDv4>",
  "name": "...",
  "duration": {"numerator": 4, "denominator": 1},
  "canvas": {"width": 1920, "height": 1080},
  "assets": [],
  "nodes": [],
  "animations": [],
  "camera": {
    "keyframes": [
      {"at": {"numerator": 0, "denominator": 1}, "zoom": 1.0},
      {"at": {"numerator": 4, "denominator": 1}, "zoom": 1.08, "pan_x": -24}
    ],
    "easing": "ease_in_out"
  }
}
```

`camera` is optional; without it the identity camera is used, so existing scenes
render unchanged. Keys carry `pan_x`/`pan_y`, `zoom` (0.25–4) and
`rotation_degrees`; they are interpolated like node animations and applied to
every resolved instruction, so preview, layout and materialisation agree.

Node kinds: `group`, `text`, `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `arrow`, `image`.

- Text needs `text`; optional `position`, `font_size`, `fill`, `spans`
  (byte-offset highlight runs).
- Rectangle and ellipse need `size`; optional `position`, `fill`, `stroke`,
  `stroke_width`, `rotation_degrees`, `opacity`.
- Image needs `asset_id`; group needs `children`.
- Colours are typed `{red, green, blue, alpha}` with 0–255 channels. There is no
  CSS string and no expression language.
- Animated properties are `translation_x`, `translation_y`, `scale`, `rotation`,
  `opacity`, `width`, `height`. Keyframes are ascending, inside `[0, duration]`,
  and each node animates a property once. Easings: `linear`, `ease_in`,
  `ease_out`, `ease_in_out`.

To change the title, a colour or a size, edit the node's fields and re-materialise.
The materialised clip already on the timeline is an ordinary video clip; re-running
the scene never silently replaces it — insert the new render and delete the old
clip only if the user asks.

## Reusable assets

Reusable scenes, fragments and image cutouts carry typed parameters for text,
colour, size, opacity and rotation (ADR 0010). `project.json` records the library,
so every verb below takes `--attach project.json` and resolves the same folder the
app shows; `--library PATH` overrides it for one call. The asset verbs never open
a project except `insert`.

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `motion asset list --attach project.json --json` | Ids, names, categories, kinds and durations. |
| `motion asset validate --file FILE` | Validate one asset document. |
| `motion asset save --attach project.json --file FILE [--category C]` | Classify and store an authored asset. |
| `motion asset instantiate --attach project.json --id ID [--values JSON] --output OUT.ormotion.json [--scene-id] [--name]` | Write a scene file from an asset; no render, no project. |
| `motion asset import --attach project.json --source IMAGE.png [--name] [--category] [--tags a,b] [--width] [--height] [--seconds]` | Add a PNG cutout asset. |
| `motion asset remove --attach project.json --id ID` | Remove one asset. |
| `motion asset insert --attach project.json --asset-id ID [--values JSON] [--at] [--track] [--output] [--frame-rate] [--width] [--height]` | Instantiate, render through the app, import and insert one clip. |

Text and choice values are strings, numbers are numbers, and colours are
`{red,green,blue,alpha}`. Only `insert` needs the running app. A scene with
library-relative image assets is inserted from the app, not by `publish`.

## Bounds

A scene file is at most 4 MiB, 4096 nodes, groups nested 16 deep, 4096
animations, 4096 keyframes per animation, 64 KiB per text node. Asset paths must
be scene-local or project-relative; remote URLs are refused. Keep scenes short:
a ten-second 30 fps scene is 300 encoded frames, and one publish materialises at
most 200,000 frames.

# Project safety

Scope: how to change a live project without losing work. Rust owns the project,
its revision and its history; every `tools/or` mutation goes through the same
validated command path as the editor.

## The one rule

Never edit a `.orproj` file or anything inside the project directory directly.
The running app holds the authoritative document; a direct edit is invisible to
it and will be overwritten or rejected. Attach through `project.json` and let the
app apply the command.

## Reading state

`tools/or project summary --attach project.json --json` returns the project name,
its ids and the live revision. The save state is a different read:
`tools/or session describe --attach project.json --json` returns `dirty` beside
the same revision, and the human form prints `Dirty: true|false`. `timeline`
queries, `media list` and `media probe` are reads: they never mutate. A rename is
`project rename --name NEW --attach project.json --json`; it is a normal edit and
is saved like any other.

Edits are live in the app as soon as the command succeeds, but they are unsaved
until `project save` runs. `dirty: false` after an edit means something is wrong;
report it instead of claiming success.

## Save and history

- Call `tools/or project save --attach project.json --json` once after finishing
  the requested change, unless the user asked to review first.
- `tools/or history undo --attach project.json --json` and
  `tools/or history redo --attach project.json --json` are the canonical history.
  They undo one project edit, not one conversation turn, so a `--apply` voiceover
  run (one import and one insert per line, plus a caption import) is several
  steps. Tell the user how many steps you undid.
- `tools/or session describe` only reports the live session. Two other verbs are
  not yours to call: `session shutdown` closes the session, and `recovery
  status|apply|discard` works on a project file outside the app. Closing,
  shutting down or recovering is the user's action.

## Refused operations

A refused command is a real answer, not a transient error:

- A time outside the sequence or a trim that inverts a clip: re-read the
  timeline and choose a valid time.
- A locked track: read `timeline tracks`, ask before unlocking it with
  `set-track-state`, then edit.
- A revision conflict: re-read `project summary`, then repeat the edit once.
- A duplicate id, a missing media id or a clip that no longer exists: re-read the
  ids and retry with real values.
- A missing CLI verb (speed, volume, freeze, styling, export): this is the app's
  surface, not a failure. Say so and let the user make that change.

Do not loop on the same failing command. After two identical failures, stop and
report the verb, its error code and the next concrete step.

## Reporting

Say what changed: track, clip, exact time. Say what was saved. Do not claim a
change that no command confirmed; a timeline read after the edit is the minimum
evidence.

# Script, narration, captions and music

Scope: turning a spoken idea into an OR edit — a written script, narration, exact
caption clips, and a generated background-music bed. Timeline mechanics are in
[timeline-editing.md](timeline-editing.md); importing files is in
[media-and-import.md](media-and-import.md); audio the user already has (recording,
noise, speech models) is in [audio-prep.md](audio-prep.md).

## Order of work

1. Decide the length, language (`vi` or `en`), audience, tone, voice, and music
   mood with the user. Do not invent a length the user did not ask for.
2. Write the script as `work/scripts/<slug>.json` (format below).
3. Validate it without speaking: `node tools/voiceover.mjs --script PATH --plan`.
4. Narrate it. Without `--apply` the tool writes `manifest.json`, the per-line
   WAV files, and `captions.srt`; with `--apply` it also imports the WAVs, places
   them on an audio track, and imports the captions.
5. Generate the music bed, import it, and place it on another audio track.
6. Add the visuals, review the timeline, then save.

## Script format

`or-assistant-script` schema 1 is a JSON object with one narration line per
scene. The narration is what the voice says; the caption is what the subtitle
shows (it defaults to the narration).

```json
{
  "format": "or-assistant-script",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "title": "Giới thiệu OR",
  "language": "vi",
  "rate": 180,
  "gap_ms": 250,
  "scenes": [
    {
      "id": "mo-dau",
      "marker": "Mở đầu",
      "narration": "Xin chào, đây là Opencut Reinforced.",
      "caption": "Xin chào, đây là OR.",
      "duration_ms": 6000
    },
    {
      "id": "dung-phim",
      "narration": "Bạn có thể dựng phim ngay trên máy.",
      "duration_ms": 5000
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | lowercase kebab-case, unique; names the WAV and the caption order |
| `narration` | the exact words spoken by `say`; required, at most 2000 bytes |
| `caption` | the subtitle text; defaults to `narration` |
| `marker` | optional timeline marker label for this scene boundary |
| `duration_ms` | the planned visual length; only used by `--plan` |

A script may also set `voice` and `language` at the top level. The script may
contain at most 300 scenes. Every field except `scenes` is optional. `rate`
defaults to 180 words per minute and `gap_ms` to 250 milliseconds between lines.

## Two narration surfaces

The app and the workspace both narrate, and they are not the same path:

- **Workspace, offline:** `tools/voiceover.mjs` speaks each line with the macOS
  `say` voice, measures the real WAV duration, and derives exact caption times.
  The voice is the script's `voice`, then the app's saved default from **Settings
  → Narration** (`narration-settings.json`, read through `project.json`), then the
  first installed Vietnamese voice on this machine. It never falls back to a
  product constant such as `Linh`.
- **App, optional cloud voices:** **Audio → Generate voiceover…** uses the voice
  chosen in **Settings → Narration**, including cloud providers. That panel holds
  the provider cards (save/test/remove a key, the Azure region, and ElevenLabs
  personal-voice creation from a recorded WAV sample with its consent checkbox),
  and the keys live in the macOS keychain. The workspace never sees a key and must
  not ask for one; when the user wants a cloud voice, they run the app action and
  the result arrives as ordinary media you can edit and save like any other.

```sh
node tools/voiceover.mjs --script work/scripts/gioi-thieu.json --plan --json
node tools/voiceover.mjs --script work/scripts/gioi-thieu.json \
  --out work/voiceover/gioi-thieu --apply --attach project.json --json
```

The tool writes one 44.1 kHz mono PCM WAV per scene, measures its real duration
from the WAV, and builds exact start/end times for every caption. `--apply`:

- reuses the first unlocked audio track that is empty, or adds one;
- imports each WAV with `media add` and inserts it with `timeline insert-clip`;
- imports `captions.srt` with `timeline import-captions`;
- leaves the project unsaved, so you can review before `project save`.

Without `--apply`, the output is the manifest, the WAVs and the SRT. Use that
when the user wants to hear the narration before it enters the timeline. The
manifest is the same shape the applied path uses:

```json
{
  "format": "or-voiceover-manifest",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "rate": 180,
  "gap_ms": 250,
  "total_ms": 6484,
  "lines": [
    {
      "scene_id": "mo-dau",
      "start_ms": 0,
      "end_ms": 3672,
      "duration_ms": 3672,
      "file": "/absolute/path/work/voiceover/gioi-thieu/mo-dau.wav",
      "caption": "Xin chào, đây là OR."
    }
  ]
}
```

The `start_ms`/`end_ms` values are the visual scene boundaries too: add markers
with `timeline add-marker` at those times if the user wants the structure
visible in the editor.

## Captions from existing audio

The narration path derives captions from the script. For audio or video the user
already has, use the app's local multilingual transcription:

```sh
tools/or captions transcribe --attach project.json --media MEDIA_ID \
  --srt-out work/captions/clip.srt --json
tools/or timeline import-captions --attach project.json \
  --file work/captions/clip.srt --json
```

This runs in the running app (a `--project` file is refused), detects Vietnamese
or English automatically, and never changes the project. The model is the one the
app has installed and selected (Base, Small, Medium, Large v3 Turbo q5 or Large
v3 Turbo), so if it reports `TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`, send the user to
**Audio → Speech model…** instead of downloading anything here. Review the cues
(the JSON carries `start_ms`, `end_ms`, `text`, and the detected `language`) before
importing; the second command creates a new caption track and one editable
caption clip per cue. Edit the SRT first if timing or wording needs correcting.

Caption style — font, size, anchor, offset, background box and text opacity —
travels with each clip and is edited in the app's Edit Caption dialog through
`timeline.clip.update`; there is no CLI verb for it. Captions from transcription
are ordinary caption clips, so the user can restyle every cue without recreating
the track.

## Music

```sh
node tools/music.mjs --out work/music/bed.wav \
  --prompt "nhạc nền nhẹ nhàng 30 giây, không trống" --json
```

The prompt is read by the same interpreter as the app's **Audio → Generate
music…** dialog: a mood word (`calm`, `warm`, `uplifting`, `tense`, `minimal`, in
Vietnamese or English), a length (`90 giây`, `2 phút`, `40s`), a tempo (`90 bpm`)
and drums on or off (`không trống`, `no drums`, `strong drums`). The JSON carries
`summary` — `calm · 62 bpm · 30 s · no drums` — which is the readback to report,
and `plan.notes` when nothing in the sentence was understood. `--variation N`
reseeds the same request. Explicit `--mood`, `--tempo`, `--duration` and `--seed`
still work and win over the prompt, so an older command line keeps its meaning.

The bed is synthesised locally, differs by `--seed`, and is royalty-free. It is
generated quiet (about −20 dB RMS, −9 dB peak) so it sits under speech; change the
clip gain in the inspector rather than regenerating louder. The app's dialog also
ducks it under a voice track in one step. To place the workspace file:

```sh
tools/or media add --attach project.json --source /absolute/path/work/music/bed.wav --json
tools/or timeline insert-clip --attach project.json --track AUDIO_TRACK \
  --media MEDIA_ID --at 0/1 --source-start 0/1 --duration 60/1 --json
```

Find the track with `timeline tracks`; add one with `timeline add-track --kind
audio` if the project has none.

## Rules and bounds

- The workspace path is offline: `say` is a system voice, the music is
  synthesised, and the transcription model is the app's local model. No cloud key
  is read or written here; cloud voices belong to the app's Settings.
- The script and generated media live under `work/`; they are not project state.
  Importing them is what makes them part of the project.
- Never claim the narration or captions are recorded or transcribed when they
  came from a written script, and never claim a cloud voice was used when the
  system voice spoke. Say which path produced them.
- One narration line should say one thing. Long paragraphs become one long
  caption and a slow clip; split them into scenes.
- `say` is macOS-only. On another platform, say the offline voice path is
  unavailable and ask whether to use an installed voice tool, rather than
  pretending the command worked.
- A `--apply` run is several commands, so it is several undo steps; report that
  instead of calling it one undoable change.

## Verification

- `node tools/voiceover.mjs --script PATH --plan --json` prints the planned
  order and timing without side effects.
- `ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of csv=p=0 FILE.wav` confirms a
  generated WAV's real length.
- `tools/or timeline tracks` and `timeline clips` confirm what `--apply` placed.
- `tools/or project save` then `project summary` confirms the edit persisted.

# Timeline editing

Scope: the exact-time timeline commands the assistant runs against the live
project. Project state is Rust-owned; read [project-safety.md](project-safety.md)
before saving or undoing.

## Order of operations

1. `tools/or project summary --attach project.json --json` — confirm a project is
   open and read its revision. `session describe` adds the `dirty` save state.
2. `tools/or timeline tracks --attach project.json --json` and
   `tools/or timeline settings --attach project.json --json` — read the track ids
   with their kind and state, and the sequence rate.
3. `tools/or timeline clips --track TRACK_ID --attach project.json --json` — read
   the clips with their start, source range and duration. One page holds at most
   100 clips: pass `--offset` while the result reports more.
4. `tools/or timeline markers --attach project.json --json` when the request
   names a marker or asks for one; markers page by `--offset` as well.
5. Use only the ids and times those calls returned. Never invent a `clip_id`,
   `track_id` or media id.
6. Make the smallest command the request needs.
7. Re-read the affected track when placement matters.
8. `tools/or project save --attach project.json --json` unless the user asked to
   review first.

## Time form

- Times are exact `NUM/DEN` seconds or decimal seconds (`2.5`).
- A clip's `--at` is its timeline start; `--source-start` addresses the media
  in-point.
- `insert-clip` has no default duration: pass `--duration` taken from the media
  metadata in [media-and-import.md](media-and-import.md).
- `--delta` on slip, roll and slide is a signed duration (`-1/8`, `3/4`).
- Do not guess a position from the prompt. The panel sends the selected clip and
  playhead as context when they exist; otherwise ask, or append after the last
  clip on the track.

## Commands

Every command below takes `--attach project.json --json` plus the flags shown.

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `timeline add-track --kind video\|audio\|text\|caption [--id ID]` | Add an empty track. |
| `timeline set-track-state --track ID --locked BOOL --visible BOOL --muted BOOL --solo BOOL` | Set a track's state; all four values are required. |
| `timeline remove-track --track ID` | Remove an empty track. |
| `timeline move-track --id ID --to INDEX` | Reorder one track. |
| `timeline insert-clip --track --media --at --source-start --duration [--id] [--mode insert\|overwrite] [--overwrite-split-id]` | Place imported media at an exact time. `insert` (the default) moves later clips right; `overwrite` clears the range, and an overwrite that lands strictly inside an existing clip must name the id for the split remainder. |
| `timeline insert-text \| insert-caption --track --at --duration --text [--id]` | Add a text clip, or a caption clip on a caption track. |
| `timeline move-clip --clip --track --at` | Move a clip in time, possibly to another track. |
| `timeline trim-clip --clip --edge start\|end --to [--ripple]` | Trim one edge to an exact timeline time; `--ripple` pulls later clips and is accepted on an end edge only. |
| `timeline slip-clip --clip --delta` | Move the source window inside a fixed clip; the clip stays where it is. |
| `timeline roll-clip --clip --delta` | Move the cut between this clip and its neighbour. |
| `timeline slide-clip --clip --delta` | Move the clip in time and let its neighbours absorb the move. |
| `timeline split-clip --clip --at [--id]` | Split a clip; the right-hand part starts there. |
| `timeline delete-clip --clip` | Delete a clip and leave the gap. |
| `timeline ripple-delete-clip --clip` | Delete a clip and close the gap on that track. |
| `timeline duck-clip --track --clip --voice-track [--duck-db N]` | Lower a music clip under a voice track in one command and one undo step. |
| `timeline import-captions --file PATH.srt\|PATH.vtt` | Add a reviewed subtitle file as a new caption track. |
| `timeline add-marker --at --label [--id]` | Add a labelled marker. |
| `timeline move-marker --id --to` / `rename-marker --id --label` / `delete-marker --id` | Change or remove a marker. |
| `timeline set-frame-rate --rate NUM/DEN` / `clear-frame-rate` | Set or unset the sequence rate. |

`tools/or commands` lists every mutating verb and `tools/or queries` every read,
with their schema versions, when the exact surface is not obvious.
`timeline snap --clip --operation move|trim-start|trim-end --at [--track]` is a
read: it returns the snap candidate the editor would use and mutates nothing.

## Track and clip rules

- Visual tracks (`video`, `text`, `caption`) carry visual clips; `audio` tracks
  carry audio clips. A text clip on a video track is refused.
- Text and caption clips need a text or caption track; create one with `add-track`
  when the timeline has none.
- A locked track refuses edits: read `timeline tracks`, unlock with
  `set-track-state` only when the user asked for the change, then edit.
- Clips cannot overlap on one track. `insert` makes room, `overwrite` replaces it.
- Track order on screen is the order `timeline tracks` returns; `move-track`
  changes it.

## Not available through the CLI

Speed/playback rate (1/16×–16×), reverse, freeze frame, clip volume, mute,
text/caption styling (font, size, anchor, offset, background box, opacity),
multi-clip group move, visual effects and transitions all travel through
`timeline.clip.update`, which has no `tools/or` verb yet. Export has no CLI verb
at all. When the user asks for one of these, say the app owns it: speed and
volume are on the timeline strip once the clip is selected, styling is in the
Edit Title/Caption dialog and the inspector, and export is the Export button.
Let the user make that change, then re-read the timeline and save only what the
commands you ran actually changed. Do not imitate speed with a trim or a split.

## Examples

Append a clip to the end of the first video track:

1. `media list` → choose the media id; `timeline clips --track TRACK_ID` → read
   the track's last clip end.
2. `timeline insert-clip --track TRACK_ID --media MEDIA_ID --at "<end>"
   --source-start 0 --duration "<media duration>"`.
3. `timeline clips --track TRACK_ID`, then `project save`.

Trim the selected clip to end at 4 s:

1. The panel context names the clip and its track.
2. `timeline trim-clip --clip CLIP_ID --edge end --to 4`.
3. Verify the duration is positive; a trim that would invert the clip is refused.

Slip the middle clip two frames later inside its own cut:

1. Read the clip page and confirm the source has room on both sides.
2. `timeline slip-clip --clip CLIP_ID --delta 1/15` for 30 fps, or the matching
   fraction of the sequence rate.
3. Re-read the clip: `timeline_start` and duration are unchanged; only the
   source range moved.

## Ducking music under narration

`tools/or timeline duck-clip --attach project.json --track MUSIC_TRACK --clip
MUSIC_CLIP --voice-track VOICE_TRACK [--duck-db -12] --json` lowers the music
clip wherever the voice track has clips. It is one command and one undo entry;
the music clip is split at the voice boundaries and the overlapping segments get
the gain. The app's Music dialog applies the same command automatically when a
voice track is selected.

# Troubleshooting

Scope: the failures the assistant can meet inside this workspace, and the next
concrete step for each. Report the cause, never a guessed success.

## `tools/or` is missing or not executable

The app writes `tools/or` when it connects to the app build. If it is absent, the
assistant cannot reach the project through the CLI. Check `or-cli.json` for the
path the app recorded, and tell the user to reconnect the assistant. Do not write
your own bridge or edit the project files.

## `--attach project.json` fails

The CLI reports that no project is open or that the endpoint is unavailable. The
app has no open project, the project.json pointer is stale, or this session is
not using the agent workspace (a project-folder or chosen-folder workspace has no
pointer to attach through).

- Ask the user to open or create a project in OR, then retry once.
- When this workspace has no `project.json`, use the `mcp__or__*` tools for the
  edit instead, and say which surface you used.

## The CLI has no verb for what was asked

Speed, reverse, freeze, clip volume, mute, text/caption styling, group move,
effects, export, recording and cloud narration are app-only. This is not a bug
and not a reason to fake the edit with a trim: tell the user which surface owns it
(the timeline strip, the inspector, the Edit Title/Caption dialog, the Audio tool,
the Export button), let them do it, then re-read the project.

## `no motion library is recorded by this session`

The CLI looked for `motion_library_path` in the pointer it attached through and
found none. The app writes that path into `project.json`, so the usual cause is a
pointer written by an older app build or a `project.json` from before this
install: reconnect the assistant (or update OR) so the app rewrites the marker,
then retry. Until then, name the library for one call:

```sh
LIB="<application support>/motion-library"   # beside the agent-workspace folder
tools/or motion asset list --library "$LIB" --json
```

`motion asset list`, `validate`, `save`, `instantiate`, `remove` and `import` take
`--attach project.json` and resolve the library from it; `--library` always
overrides. `motion asset insert` needs `--attach`, because it renders through the
live app.

## `publish` refuses a scene

`motion publish` accepts vector scenes only. A scene with image `assets` is
published from the app's Motion panel, which copies the images into the library.
A scene that fails validation reports `MOTION_SCENE_INVALID` with the diagnostic
codes; fix the scene, validate again, then publish once.

Without `--no-library`, `publish` saves the scene to the library the pointer
records and then renders and inserts it. Pass `--no-library` when the library copy
is not wanted, so the result is predictable.

## A motion CLI verb is not available

`tools/or motion publish` and the motion asset `insert` verb need a running OR app
with this workspace's `project.json`. If the verb itself is missing, the app build
is older than the workspace: ask the user to update OR, and use the
`mcp__or__motion_*` fallback only until then. If the app is not connected, the
CLI can still validate a scene and render a file to disk, but nothing can be
imported or inserted; tell the user insertion needs the open app and stop.

## Materialisation is slow

`motion publish` encodes every frame with the app's encoder. A short scene
still takes seconds to minutes. Wait for the tool result; do not start a second
render and do not retry after a timeout without checking whether the clip
appeared. If a render fails, read the returned code, fix the scene, and retry
once.

## Scene validation codes

Common codes and their fix:

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `MOTION_INVALID_SCENE_ID` | `scene_id` must be a fresh UUIDv4. |
| `MOTION_INVALID_DURATION` | `duration` must be greater than zero. |
| `MOTION_MISSING_TEXT` / `MOTION_MISSING_SIZE` | Add the field the node kind requires. |
| `MOTION_KEYFRAMES_UNSORTED` / `MOTION_KEYFRAME_OUT_OF_RANGE` | Sort keyframes and keep them inside the duration. |
| `MOTION_ANIMATION_UNKNOWN_NODE` | The `node_id` must exist in `nodes`. |
| `MOTION_REMOTE_ASSET_REFUSED` | Use a scene-local or project-relative asset path. |

## Transcription fails

- `local transcription needs the running app; pass --attach project.json` — the
  verb was given `--project FILE`. Transcription is a host service; attach the
  live session.
- `TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` — no model is installed, or this build has no
  whisper runtime. Send the user to **Audio → Speech model…** (or
  `scripts/install_local_transcription_helpers.sh` for a local debug build) and
  stop. Never download weights from the workspace.
- `captions transcribe` is slow on long media; one job at a time, then review the
  cues before importing them.

## `media clean-audio` or `media probe` reports a helper error

Both run the packaged FFmpeg helper. A plain debug CLI may not find it: say the
helper is missing and point the user at the app, which imports and cleans audio
through the bridge. Do not retry with guessed helper paths.

## A command is refused

See [project-safety.md](project-safety.md). Re-read state, retry once with real
ids and times, then report the refusal if it repeats.

# Review gates

Run these before rendering and again before saving. Each gate is a question, not
a checkbox you can tick by habit.

## 1. Story gate (per beat)

* If this beat were cut, would the viewer lose information, understanding or a
  memorable moment? If not, rewrite or delete it.
* Does the beat answer "what happens, why, and what comes out of it" — not just
  "what exists"?
* Is the previous beat's idea different from this one in *viewpoint* (user view,
  close-up, inside, comparison), not only in colour?

## 2. Sound-off gate

* Mute the audio. Can you still tell what is happening? A beat where only text
  appears and disappears fails this gate.
* Does the narration name a thing that is actually on screen at that moment?
  Generic animation under specific words is a fail.

## 3. Sync gate

* Does each caption appear at or after the voice reaches that phrase? Nothing may
  lead the read.
* Do captions sit in the reserved strip and never cover the illustration?
* Are cue lines short enough to stay on one line (≤ ~46 characters)?

## 4. Narration gate

* Does any line claim a feature or number that was not verified in the repo docs
  or the running app?
* Are paid services described as paid? Only free/local things may be called free.
* Is every technical term explained at the moment it is needed, in plain words?

## 5. Assembly gate

* Do the tracks end together (narration ≈ music ≈ video)?
* Are there zero gaps and zero overlaps on the video track?
* Does every marker sit on a beat boundary?
* Did you save explicitly, and does `project summary` show the new revision?

## 6. Honesty gate (reporting)

* Say which steps were verified in this session and which were not.
* Never claim the narration was listened to, or the video watched, if it wasn't.
* Never claim a harness or provider is supported unless the build's code and docs
  show it.

# OR video pipeline — reusable template

A packaged version of the workflow used to build the Opencut Reinforced explainer:
local narration → beat-planned MotionScene illustrations with baked captions →
parallel render → one assembly pass into the open project.

Nothing here changes the OR engine. It drives the app through `tools/or`, the
app's local TTS server and the deterministic MotionScene renderer.

## Contents

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `scripts/new-video.mjs` | Scaffold `videos/<slug>/` with `script.json` + `video.config.json` |
| `scripts/narration.mjs` | Local TTS → atempo → measured manifest + caption cues |
| `scripts/build-scenes.mjs` | Beat map → one MotionScene per beat (captions baked in) |
| `scripts/render.mjs` | Materialise every beat in parallel (files only, no project writes) |
| `scripts/assemble.mjs` | Clear tracks, import narration + music, duck, insert beats, markers |
| `lib/world.mjs` | Drawing kit: canvas, palette, primitives, camera presets, captions |
| `lib/composers.mjs` | 19 beat compositions (see `beats/beat-library.json`) |
| `beats/beat-library.json` | What each composition is for — pick by idea, not by habit |
| `CHECKLIST.md` | Story, sync and visual review gates |

## The five steps

Run everything from the OR workspace root (the folder with `project.json` and
`tools/or`). `$V` is your video folder.

```sh
node templates/video-pipeline/scripts/new-video.mjs --slug my-video --title "My video"

# 1. write the script (one line per spoken sentence) and the beat map
$EDITOR videos/my-video/script.json videos/my-video/video.config.json

# 2. narration at 1.6× with a completeness guard + cue timing
node templates/video-pipeline/scripts/narration.mjs --video videos/my-video --attach project.json

# 3. check the read before spending render time
node tools/music.mjs --out videos/my-video/build/music/bed.wav \
  --prompt "<mood, bpm, drums, seconds>" --json

# 4. beats → scenes → rendered clips (3 workers is a good default)
node templates/video-pipeline/scripts/build-scenes.mjs --video videos/my-video
node templates/video-pipeline/scripts/render.mjs --video videos/my-video --workers 3 --attach project.json

# 5. import everything into the open project, then save
node templates/video-pipeline/scripts/assemble.mjs --video videos/my-video --attach project.json --dry-run
node templates/video-pipeline/scripts/assemble.mjs --video videos/my-video --attach project.json
tools/or project save --attach project.json --json
```

`--dry-run` prints the tracks it will use, the beat timings and the marker count
without touching the project.

## Config shape

```jsonc
{
  "slug": "my-video",
  "title": "My video",
  "tempo": 1.6,                       // narration time-stretch (1.0 = natural)
  "gap_ms": 120,                      // silence between narration lines
  "canvas": { "width": 1920, "height": 1080 },
  "captions": { "band": 952, "font": 28, "baked": true },   // baked = no caption track
  "music": { "file": "videos/my-video/build/music/bed.wav", "duckDb": -12 },
  "beats": [
    { "id": "open",      "composer": "open",      "camera": "push", "lines": ["mo-dau"] },
    { "id": "assembly",  "composer": "assembly",  "camera": "pull", "lines": ["y-tuong"] },
    { "id": "close",     "composer": "close",     "camera": "push", "lines": ["ket"] }
  ]
}
```

* `lines` are the `id`s from `script.json`. A beat owns consecutive lines; the
  scene lasts until the next beat starts, so narration never plays over the
  wrong picture. Lines left out of every beat are reported by
  `build-scenes.mjs` — fix them, don't ignore them.
* `camera`: `push`, `pull`, `pan`, `fly` or `none`. Change it between beats.
* `composer`: any key in `beats/beat-library.json`.

## Rules the template already enforces

* **Captions never lead the voice.** The first chunk of a line starts exactly at
  the measured audio start; later chunks start at their character-proportional
  position plus 130 ms, and every cue is clamped to the next cue's start.
* **No line can lose words.** A line that comes back shorter than 80 % of the
  expected duration for its text is re-spoken sentence by sentence and stitched.
* **Beat boundaries are exact.** Beats tile the whole narration: no gaps, no
  overlapping clips.
* **Renders are revision-safe.** `render.mjs` only writes files; every project
  write happens in `assemble.mjs`, sequentially.
* **Captions are baked** into the scene strip by default, so the timeline carries
  no caption track and nothing covers the illustration.

## Segment shape that works

One beat = one idea = 8–20 s. Sequence:

1. hook (result or question) — `open`
2. the discovery, one concrete action at a time — `chatLink`, `chatRun`,
   `assembly`, `voiceGen`, `whisperListen`
3. the mechanism behind it — `motionDetail`, `layers`, `previewSync`
4. the payoff — `finale`
5. one takeaway — `close`

Do not stack two diagram beats in a row; alternate user view, close-up,
inside-view and comparison.

## Timing budget

Narration at 1.6× runs about **28 characters per second**. For a 5-minute video:

```
chars ≈ 300 s × 28 ≈ 8,400 characters  (≈ 60–75 spoken lines)
```

Add `gap_ms × lines` for the real total, then check `manifest.total_ms` before
rendering. Too short: add mechanism lines, not filler. Too long: cut a beat.

## Pitfalls that cost time (already handled, but know them)

* A media item caches the duration it was imported with. If you re-render a file
  in place, remove that media item before re-inserting, or the clip keeps the old
  length.
* `insert-clip --duration` must not exceed the media duration; the template floors
  to whole milliseconds.
* Exact rationals with huge denominators are rejected by the CLI; keep
  `n/d` reduced or use milliseconds.
* Materialisation validates more strictly than `motion validate`. Text nodes that
  overlap each other or sit on identical lines can trip `MOTION_INVALID_TEXT_SIZE`
  at render time — keep labels apart.
* Editing the project while renders are running causes revision conflicts. That
  is why render and assemble are separate steps.
* Three parallel workers is the sweet spot; more workers mostly add contention.

## A worked example

`videos/example-opencut/` holds the script and beat map of the shipped explainer
(74 lines, 19 beats, 4:46 at tempo 1.6). No media is stored there — point
`music.file` at a bed you generated and run the five steps to rebuild it from
scratch, or copy the structure for a new video.

## Provenance

Built from `work/local-tts-v4.mjs` and `work/build-scenes-v6.mjs`, the exact
generators used for the shipped explainer (74 narration lines, 19 beats, 4:46,
baked captions, tense bed). The live project and those files are left untouched.

# Workspace tools

Scope: the local commands this workspace exposes. `tools/or` is the default way
to read and change the open project; `mcp__or__*` tools are the fallback for
motion insertion, the motion library, and a CLI failure. Some operations belong to
the app alone — speed, volume, styling, export, recording, cloud voices — and
have no verb here on purpose.

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `tools/or <verb> --attach project.json --json` | The OR CLI bound to the running app build. Reads and edits the live project through the app-written pointer. `tools/or commands` and `tools/or queries` list the verbs. |
| `tools/or media clean-audio --source IN --out OUT` | Offline noise reduction; writes a new file that you import to use. |
| `tools/or captions transcribe` | Transcribe one media item locally (Vietnamese/English auto-detected); needs the running app. |
| `tools/or timeline import-captions` | Apply a reviewed SRT/WebVTT file as a new caption track. |
| `tools/or motion ...` | Validate, inspect, evaluate, layout, render, from-code, materialize or publish a scene. `publish` saves it to the library, renders, imports **and** inserts in one call. |
| `tools/or motion asset ...` | List, validate, save, instantiate, import, remove or insert from the app's motion library; pass `--attach project.json` and the CLI resolves the folder from the pointer. |
| `node tools/motion-scaffold.mjs` | Write a valid V1 `.ormotion.json` skeleton into `scenes/`. |
| `node tools/voiceover.mjs` | Speak an `or-assistant-script` with the macOS voice, write exact timings and SRT, optionally import and place the result. |
| `node tools/music.mjs` | Synthesise a quiet, royalty-free background music bed offline, from a prompt or explicit flags. |

The app keeps its motion library at `<application support>/motion-library`, and the
workspace `project.json` records that path, so every motion verb resolves it from
`--attach project.json`. `--library PATH` overrides it for one call.

## Examples

```sh
tools/or project summary --attach project.json --json
tools/or timeline tracks --attach project.json --json
tools/or timeline clips --track TRACK_ID --attach project.json --json
tools/or timeline markers --attach project.json --json
tools/or media list --attach project.json --json
tools/or media clean-audio --source /absolute/in.wav --out /absolute/out.wav --json
tools/or project save --attach project.json --json
tools/or motion validate --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --json
tools/or motion inspect --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --json
tools/or motion evaluate --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --at 1/2 --json
tools/or motion layout --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --at 1/2 --json
tools/or motion from-code --source work/sample.rs --output scenes/sample.ormotion.json
tools/or motion render --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --at 1/2 --output work/title.png
tools/or motion publish --attach project.json --scene scenes/title.ormotion.json --json
tools/or motion asset list --attach project.json --json
tools/or motion asset insert --attach project.json --asset-id ASSET_ID --json
node tools/voiceover.mjs --script work/scripts/demo.json --plan --json
node tools/voiceover.mjs --script work/scripts/demo.json --out work/voiceover/demo --apply --attach project.json --json
node tools/music.mjs --out work/music/bed.wav --prompt "nhạc nền nhẹ nhàng 30 giây, không trống" --json
tools/or captions transcribe --attach project.json --media MEDIA_ID --srt-out work/captions/clip.srt --json
tools/or timeline import-captions --attach project.json --file work/captions/clip.srt --json
```

`motion publish` needs the running app: it validates the scene, saves it as a
reusable library asset, renders it, imports the video and inserts an ordinary clip
through validated commands. Pass `--no-library` to skip the asset save on purpose.
`motion materialize` only writes a file; use it when a file is the goal, not as an
insertion path. The MCP motion tools are a fallback for a CLI failure, not the
default.

## Bounds

- `tools/or` is written by the app on connect; editing it is pointless.
- Scaffold and CLI write only the files you name; nothing else is project state.
- No workspace tool reads a cloud key. Narration keys live in the macOS keychain
  and belong to the app's Settings → Narration panel.
